findings.detail: Wave 4 runs Task 9 and Task 10 in parallel, and BOTH list `frontend/i18n/locales/uk.json` and `frontend/i18n/locales/en.json` in their 'Files to modify'. Two parallel tasks editing the same locale files will produce merge conflicts (and risk i18n parity-gate breakage). Fix: either (a) move Task 10 to a Wave 5 after Task 9, (b) merge Tasks 9 and 10 into one frontend task, or (c) carve i18n key additions into a single dedicated task/owner so only one task in the wave writes uk.json/en.json.

Several implementation-task descriptions are dense and run beyond the recommended 2-3 sentence scope statement, embedding behavioral detail that belongs in task files at decomposition time. Most notable: Task 6 (FunnelExecutionEngine) packs the full step-runner algorithm (atomic-claim, dispatch table, pre-send gate, bot-pin, per-step state machine, send-fail semantics) into one description; Task 5 and Task 7 are similarly detailed. These read more like mini-designs than scope lines. They contain no AC/TDD-anchors/line-numbers (good), and the detail is accurate, so this is advisory, not blocking. Consider trimming each to WHAT/WHY + a Decision reference and letting task-decomposition expand the HOW.
